If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and the required wake-visual skill, then inspect the current rollout evidence and inherited guidance before touching the policy. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace.

The visual-first skill requires anchoring the images to observations and metrics before any edit. I’m now inventorying all sampled examples and inherited optimizer logs, then I’ll compare the best finite result with the most informative failure.

The sampled results are all left-domain failures, but they separate mechanisms clearly: stronger direct heading-rate damping gives the best upstream progress, while the first lateral-velocity correction loses that gain. I’m inspecting the common prewarm and released trajectories now to identify which correction sign/topology is physically supported.

The image/diagnostic cross-check shows the `0.70` turn-rate gain is genuinely the strongest sample: it reaches `5.33L` with mean upstream speed `-0.130`, and even avoids the exact posterior angle stop (`44.1°` versus `45°`). Yet the same upper-loop exit, both rate/command caps, and higher loads remain. That rules out treating the hard posterior angle stop alone as the cause; I’m checking inherited trials for the cleanest untested way to soften the persistent geometric steering request.

The selected single hypothesis is to keep the best sampled `0.70` heading-rate damping and reduce only the posterior steering ceiling from `10°` to `8°`. This targets the persistent mean bend after yaw damping subsides, while preserving the entire upstream-capable oscillator; I’m recording that diagnosis before editing, as the visual-first skill requires.

The candidate and both required evidence files are now updated. I’ve also distilled the new reusable boundary: `0.70` improves approach but not the loop, while the sampled lateral-velocity damper measurably degrades the `0.35` controller. Next I’m running the mandated contract checker and will repair anything it flags; no CFD will be run here.
